headline: This law lets the federal government lease back buildings on federal property it has sold, for up to three years, to help complete the sale.
what_it_does: It amends the Federal Assets Sale and Transfer Act of 2016. Under the change, existing improvements on a property sold under that Act can be leased back to the federal government for up to three years. The stated purpose is to make the sale easier to complete.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that occupy federal real property being sold
who_it_affects.how: They may be able to keep using existing buildings on a sold property by leasing them back for up to three years.

who_it_affects.group: Buyers of federal real property sold under the Federal Assets Sale and Transfer Act of 2016
who_it_affects.how: A sale may include a leaseback of existing improvements to the federal government for up to three years, so the buyer may not get immediate use of those improvements.
